interfaces.name: hel_dz
interfaces.constraints: Aligned float64 direction indicator in caller length units: axial difference, or for equal-height points pitch times transverse rotation sign. Zero is possible, including coincident points. This is not a unit vector or probability. The symbolic expression covers only the axial-difference branch; no symbolic fallback proof is claimed.

providers.operation: Determine axial motion sense from two positions, a transverse center and signed pitch, including the equal-height rotation fallback.
providers.plain_description: Determine the direction of travel along a spiral from two points.
providers.validity_bounds: Nonempty aligned finite float64 vector. Coordinates, centers and pitch share a caller-defined length unit. No broadcasting. Qualified domain excludes nonfinite intermediate arithmetic; point pairs and center define the caller-selected transverse rotation sense. Aligned float64 direction indicator in caller length units: axial difference, or for equal-height points pitch times transverse rotation sign. Zero is possible, including coincident points. This is not a unit vector or probability. The symbolic expression covers only the axial-difference branch; no symbolic fallback proof is claimed.
providers.reuse: Numeric geometry with caller-defined coordinates and units; detector topology, field strength and tracking policy remain outside the provider.

symbolic_scope: Axial-difference branch only; equal-height fallback checked concretely.
limitations: Automated Tier3 qualification only; no human Tier1 or usage-qualified Tier2 designation.
Nonempty aligned finite float64 vectors in consistent caller-defined length units. No general broadcasting contract.
Output is axial difference except at equal heights, where it is pitch times transverse rotation sign. Zero is possible and callers must handle it.
The existing provider does not independently enforce every shape, dtype or finite-intermediate precondition. Qualified callers must enforce these conditions.
Finite input can overflow the fallback cross product while yielding a finite sign. Such arithmetic is outside qualification; no floating-point error bound is supplied.
The registered symbolic equation describes only the ordinary axial-difference branch. The abstract witness supplies shape only; neither proves the equal-height fallback.
Geometry is reusable across applications with consistent coordinates and units. No detector layout, field strength, candidate ranking or calibration map is embedded.
Installed RECORD integrity validates current dependency files, not wheel publisher authentication or deployment on other platforms.
Legacy approval and history remain preserved. Canonical approval, recipe integration and original-CDG publication are separate gates.
